newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN INTERBANK RATE ENDS DOWN ON C. BANK MOVE.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN INTERBANK RATE ENDS DOWN ON C. BANK MOVE.

text.p: Taiwan's recently rising interbank rate ended lower on Tuesday after the central bank injected T$35 billion worth of funds into the banking system to alleviate tight liquidity, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 9.789 percent against Monday's 9.852 end -- but still well above the central bank's previously declared 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper stabilised at 8.75-9.00 percent.
Dealers said the central bank's move helped ease current liquidity squeeze, and they expected the bank to continue to inject funds into the banking system through open market operations on Wednesday.
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was stable at 6.1320 percent in late trade.
Buying interest in the bond market increased as the stock market's recent consolidation triggered short-term speculative buying, dealers said.
